text: F-strings do far more than drop variables into text — they have a rich formatting mini-language.
After a colon, you can control alignment and width — less-than for left, greater-than for right.
So you can line up names and scores into neat columns, perfect for tables.
[chuckle] Numbers get powerful formatting too — dot-one-f rounds to one decimal place.
[sniff] A percent sign formats a fraction as a percentage, and a comma adds thousands separators automatically.
So a big number like one-point-two million prints with commas, instantly readable.
[sigh] The equals specifier is a debugging gem — it prints both the variable's name and its value.
That single trick replaces countless print statements while you hunt down a bug.
[groan] And you can run real expressions and method calls right inside the braces — f-strings are tiny programs in a string.
